correctness.rationale: For K=B_2^d+[-s,s]e1, h_K(theta)=1+s|theta1| and volume is κ_d+2sκ_(d-1), so the polar is an explicit positive spherical-coordinate integral. Integration by parts and an increasing-function covariance prove strict monotonicity; Taylor expansion proves a positive quadratic ball-end deficit. Beta-integral asymptotics give d>=3 powers, while an elementary d=2 angular integral gives logarithmic second-order tail. Half-normal convergence at s=tau/sqrt(d) and dominated convergence at fixed s>0 give the noncommuting high-dimensional limits. Independently integrated d=2,3,4,6,10 at multiple s; checked planar closed form at s=3,10,30.
